title: Four classes, four verdicts

prereqs.why: The partition into classes and the class properties are exactly what each row has to be decided by.
Recurrent or transient is the first half of each verdict.
Period is the second half, and one of the classes has period two.

statement:
A Markov chain on $S = \{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$ has these transitions (every
arrow not listed has probability $0$):

$$\begin{aligned}
&p_{1,2} = 1 &\quad& p_{2,1} = 1\\
&p_{3,1} = \tfrac12 && p_{3,4} = \tfrac12\\
&p_{4,4} = \tfrac12 && p_{4,5} = \tfrac12\\
&p_{5,4} = 1\\
&p_{6,3} = \tfrac12 && p_{6,6} = \tfrac12
\end{aligned}$$

The communicating classes are $\{1,2\}$, $\{3\}$, $\{4,5\}$ and $\{6\}$.

Match each class to the correct verdict. One verdict on the right fits none
of them, and in fact describes something that cannot happen at all.
hints: A class is **closed** when no arrow leaves it. Check each of the four for an escape route.
A finite closed class is recurrent, and a class that is not closed is transient. That settles all four immediately.
For period: from state 1 the chain can only be back at 1 after an even number of steps. From state 4 it can be back after one step.
The verdict that fits nothing is the one that contradicts a theorem in the notes: every recurrent class is closed.

right: Closed and recurrent, and periodic with period 2: returns happen only at even times.
Transient, and the chain leaves it on the very next step whichever way it goes.
Closed and recurrent, and aperiodic, because one of its states can be returned to in a single step.
Transient, though the chain may linger: a self-loop keeps it there for a geometric number of steps and then it leaves for good.
